title: COVID-19-associated alterations of brain structure and functional connectomics
summary:
SARS-CoV-2 infections may be associated with long-term effects that persist weeks and months after the infection. Apart from cardiac and muscular problems, these include a wide variety of neurological symptoms such as impaired concentration, anosmia, fatigue, sleep disorder, anxiety and depressive symptoms. After initial epidemiologic analyses of these long-term changes, a growing body of research is now aiming at disentangling the physiological mechanisms underlying the symptoms. While many of these studies consider immunologic aspects, it remains unclear if the described long-term symptoms are associated with structural and functional changes of the brain.
We now aim to use measures to assess individual functional connectivity changes accompanied with assessments of structural brain changes that might be underlying COVID-19-associated neurological symptoms.
conditions: Contact with and exposure to other communicable diseases

interventions.name: The target population of our study includes previously collected data from patients in the National Pandemic Cohort Network (NAPKON) High Resolution Platform (HAP) cohort in the recovery phase of COVID-19 disease, focusing on cranial MRI data at various time points. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
All patients (age >18 years, no restrictions regarding gender and ethnic origin) who were examined as part of the NAPKON HAP cohort (as a result of a proven (PCR test) COVID-19 disease) and underwent one or more cranial MRI scan will included in the analysis.
Exclusion criteria:
- Patients without cranial MRI examination 
- Lack of proof of COVID-19 disease
- Contraindication for MR imaging (metal, renal insufficiency, lack of compliance)
